papers.title: From cacophony to hierarchy: a principled framework for assessing AI consciousness
papers.abstract: The question of AI consciousness is one of the most urgent pre-emptive problems in philosophy and computer science, yet progress is hampered by a cacophony of competing theories that often talk past each other. Separating the hard problem from the mapping problem allows the deepest metaphysical disagreements to be set aside: granting that experience supervenes on a system's organisation, the tractable question becomes at which grain of description that supervenience base sits. We extend Marr's three levels of analysis into a five-level hierarchy of functional descriptions (behavioural, computational, intrinsic causal-structural, organismic, and organism-environment) grounded in supervenience, coarse-graining, and multiple realisability. The major theories of consciousness are positioned within this hierarchy according to which level they take to be critical, and for each level we develop operationalisable indicators and assess current AI systems against them. A Bayesian model then combines theoretical credences with indicator evidence into an overall credence in a system's capacity for consciousness. In illustrative assessments, the verdict for current LLMs is driven as much by where theoretical credence is placed as by how the evidence is read: under different stipulated readings and credence distributions, assessments range from below 0.01 to roughly 0.8, showing sensitivity to assumptions. Finally, the consciousness indicators at each level closely overlap with the architectural features needed for general intelligence, suggesting that increasingly capable AI may become a stronger candidate for consciousness. The framework supports a structured agnosticism, in which theoretical commitments are made explicit, credences are updated as evidence accumulates, and assessments take the form of aggregated probabilities rather than verdicts.

papers.title: Transformative Effects of Mindfulness Meditation Training on the Dynamic Reconfiguration of Executive and Default Mode Networks in Internet Gaming Disorder
papers.abstract: Background Internet gaming disorder (IGD) is a pervasive global mental health issue, and finding effective treatments for the disorder has been challenging. Mindfulness meditation (MM), recognized for its holistic approach that involves integrating mental and physical facets, holds promise for addressing the multifaceted nature of addiction. Nevertheless, the effect of MM on IGD and its associated neural networks, particularly in terms of their dynamic characteristics, remains elusive. Methods A total of 61 eligible participants with IGD (30 in the MM group, 31 in the progressive muscle relaxation [PMR] group) completed the experimental protocol, which involved pretest, an 8-session MM/PMR training regimen, and posttests. The 142 brain regions of interest were categorized into 5 brain networks using dynamic network reconfiguration analysis based on Shen’s functional template. A comparative analysis of network dynamic features, including recruitment and integration coefficients, was performed across different groups and tests using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data. Results While clinically nonspecific effects were observed in the PMR group, the MM group exhibited a significant reduction in addiction severity and cravings. In the dynamic brain network, MM training increased the recruitment coefficient within the frontoparietal network (FPN) and basal ganglia network (BGN) but decreased it within the default mode network (DMN). Furthermore, MM training increased the integration coefficient in the FPN-DMN and DMN–limbic network (LN). Conclusions MM has demonstrated pronounced efficacy in treating IGD. MM may enhance top-down control functions, cognitive and emotional functions, and reward-system processing, potentially through the reconfiguration of the FPN-DMN pathway, DMN-LN pathway, and BGN.

papers.title: Understanding the psycho-neuro-endocrine-immunology pathways in glaucoma and their modulation by mindfulness meditation.
papers.abstract: Glaucoma is among the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. It is increasingly being recognized as a complex and multifactorial disease with diverse pathogenesis. Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) remains the primary modifiable risk factor and continues to be the cornerstone of current glaucoma management. The accumulating evidence provided clinical insights that factor beyond IOP may also influence disease onset and progression. In the recent era, chronic stress has emerged out to be one such factor and has been linked to alteration in neuroendocrine, autonomic, and inflammatory pathways. The evolving concept of Psycho-Neuro-Endocrine-Immunology (PNEI) provides an integrative framework to examine these interactions and their possible relevance to glaucoma pathophysiology. The narrative review was carried out on existing evidence that relates biology of stress to glaucoma within the framework of "PNEI" and "Allostatic load." In addition, it will also explore the potential role of mindfulness meditation to serve as a nonpharmacological adjunct capable of modulating key PNEI pathways, which include cortisol regulation, autonomic balance, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress. The evidence available to date is encouraging regarding the effects of mindfulness-based interventions. However, the current literature is limited by considerable variability in study designs, intervention protocol, outcome measures, and duration of follow-up. Larger prospective studies with standardized intervention and longer follow-up are needed to clarify the role of mindfulness-based intervention in glaucoma care. Integration of PNEI-based approaches may offer a conceptual framework for future research in holistic glaucoma care, pending validation of long-term clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Mental Health Support and Educational Programs for New Graduate Nurses: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: AimTo explore studies on mental health support and educational programs for new graduate nurses to enhance their workplace adaptation, job satisfaction, and well-being.BackgroundNew graduate nurses face significant mental health challenges during the transition to practice, contributing to high turnover rates.MethodsThis scoping review used Arksey and O'Malley's framework and Joanna Briggs Institute's methodology to identify quantitative and mixed-methods studies in English or Japanese, published between January 2014 and July 2024, involving new graduate nurses within 12 months of graduation.ResultsOf 1,024 records, 14 studies were included. The analysis identified three categories of mental health support programs (clinical nurse educator-led mentorship, mindfulness-based interventions, and workplace environment support) and four types of educational programs (resilience education, communication skills training, positive psychology interventions, and stress management education). Research gaps included limited evidence regarding long-term effectiveness and the lack of standardized measurement tools.ConclusionExisting programs show promise; however, researchers need to conduct rigorous, longitudinal, multisite studies using standardized measurement tools, along with research that evaluates program sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and cultural adaptability.

papers.title: Interoception in psychiatry: A systematic scoping review on concepts, methods and clinical impact.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Interoception - the perception and interpretation of internal bodily signals - is increasingly recognized as a transdiagnostic mechanism underlying emotion regulation and psychopathology. Although many psychiatric interventions implicitly or explicitly target interoceptive processes, there is limited clarity regarding how interoception is defined, measured, and applied in mental healthcare, as well as how effective interoception-focused interventions are across psychiatric populations. METHODS: A systematic scoping review was conducted of peer-reviewed studies published up to September 1, 2025, using Scopus, PsycINFO, and Web of Science. Studies were included if they evaluated interventions targeting interoception or related constructs in individuals with psychiatric disorders. Studies focusing on emotional awareness, emotion regulation, or alexithymia were excluded. Data were synthesized to map definitions, measurements, intervention types, effectiveness, and reported benefits and barriers. RESULTS: Forty-seven studies were included (37 quantitative; 13 qualitative/mixed). There was substantial heterogeneity in conceptualization and measurement, with most studies focusing on interoceptive awareness using self-report measures, particularly the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA). Interventions included mindfulness-based approaches, body-oriented therapies, structured protocols, and technology-supported methods. Of 37 (quasi-)experimental studies, 34 reported significant improvements in interoceptive outcomes. Qualitative findings highlighted benefits such as improved body awareness and emotion regulation, alongside barriers including skepticism, difficulty engaging with bodily focus, and feelings of being overwhelmed. CONCLUSIONS: Interoception-focused interventions show consistent positive effects across psychiatric populations and represent a promising avenue for clinical practice. However, variability in definitions and measurement currently limits translation into standardized care. Future research should prioritize clearer conceptualization, multi-method assessment strategies, and greater attention to individual differences to support more personalized and effective interoception-based treatments.

papers.title: A Rapid Review of Conventional and Strengths-Based Interventions to Support Recovery for Adult Female Survivors of Sexual Assault.
papers.abstract: Sexual violence remains a major public health issue with serious consequences for adult female survivors of sexual assault (AFSSA). This review examined recent evidence on conventional and strengths-based therapies for AFSSA and identified key intervention components that aid recovery. Guided by Cochrane Rapid Review Procedures and PRISMA standards, nine databases and reference lists were searched for peer-reviewed studies in English from 2012 to 2022 that met eligibility criteria for interventions targeting AFSSA. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts using the Rayyan tool, resolving discrepancies with a third reviewer. Data were extracted, appraised using JBI tools, and findings were synthesized using a narrative approach. Characterizing eating behavioral phenotypes in mood disorders: A cross-sectional investigation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maladaptive eating behaviors in mood disorders are diverse and clinically relevant but have only been characterized into phenotypes based on theoretical evidence. The objective of the current study is to assess the prevalence of maladaptive eating behavior phenotypes (EBP) in mood disorders based on empirical evidence. METHODS: An online survey package including five questionnaires was administered to assess the prevalence and proportion of maladaptive eating behaviors in a mood disorder population ( RESULTS: Numerous maladaptive eating behaviors were identified in MDD and BD, including poor dietary quality, emotional eating, binge eating, and night eating behaviors. Differences between diagnostic groups are discussed. Three EBPs were characterized according to the PCA: (1) food impulsivity; (2) emotional eating; and (3) mindfulness in eating, with a significant influence of age and medication on the characterizations according to the mANOVA. CONCLUSIONS: Maladaptive eating behaviors occur in mood disorders and can be characterized into distinct EBPS. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis-generating given the sample size, absence of a healthy comparator group, and potential confounds. As psychiatry moves toward a more comprehensive, personalized approach to diagnosis and treatment, EBPs require prospective validation in larger, controlled investigations to determine clinical relevance.

papers.title: A Short Spirituality Scale Grounded in the Bhagavad Gita: Development and Validation in India.
papers.abstract: Spirituality is increasingly recognized for its association with emotional and physical health. However, many existing measures conflate it with general well-being or religiosity, making it difficult to examine spirituality as a distinct construct. The present study introduces the Short Spirituality Scale (SSS) to address this problem. It consists of a ten-item spirituality measure grounded in the Bhagavad Gita's four paths of spiritual growth-karma (selfless action), jñāna (discernment), dhyāna (meditation), and bhakti (devotion). Textual analysis, expert input, and cognitive interviewing were used to develop the items to enhance clarity, inclusiveness, and cultural sensitivity. Although items were written to represent the four yogic paths, psychometric analyses consistently supported a stable two-factor structure-Acceptance of Divine Presence and Abidance in the Absolute. Exploratory (N = 204) and confirmatory (N = 277) factor analyses showed strong model fit. Reliability analyses demonstrated good internal consistency, high test-retest stability, and moderate inter-rater agreement. Validity testing (N = 417) found that higher spirituality correlated with better life satisfaction and flourishing. Higher spirituality scores were also negatively associated with burnout, depression, stress, anxiety, and neuroticism, supporting strong concurrent, convergent, divergent, and discriminant validity. Preliminary percentile-based reference values from an adult sample (N = 1,682) provide age- and gender-specific interpretation. The SSS fills a critical methodological gap by offering one of the few spirituality measures grounded in a coherent philosophical framework rather than fragmented or atheoretical item pools. It assesses spirituality as an orientation toward transcendence rather than as well-being and is potentially useful in mental health practice, public health programs, and spiritual care.

papers.title: Protocol for a Multimodal Investigation of Interoception in Adolescence and Testing Virtual Reality Interventions to Improve Interoceptive Impairments.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychiatric conditions predominantly emerge in adolescence and represent a leading cause of disability and morbidity worldwide. Interoceptive dysfunction has been implicated in the development and maintenance of several psychiatric conditions and is characterized by disruptions in the perception and interpretation of internal bodily signals. Despite its recognized importance, interoception has not been well-characterized in adolescence-a key developmental period marked by profound neurobiological, physiological, and psychosocial change. Consequently, the precise role of interoceptive dysfunction in the onset and progression of psychiatric disorders remains unclear. Thus, research is needed to characterize interoception in adolescence, elucidate its contributions to psychiatric conditions, and determine interventions that effectively address interoceptive impairments. Importantly, such interventions should be designed with future dissemination in mind-prioritizing accessibility, scalability, and standardization. Virtual reality (VR) represents one promising approach to deliver therapeutic skills that target interoception, which also engages multiple sensory systems (e.g., visual, auditory, bodily signals) during intervention delivery. These immersive and controllable experiences provide a unique platform to systematically target interoceptive processes when delivering evidence-based therapeutic strategies such as mindfulness and relaxation training. By enabling standardized delivery and precise manipulation of multisensory experiences, VR may overcome key barriers to the dissemination and scalability of traditional approaches to intervention. OBJECTIVE: This project conducts a multimodal assessment of interoception and related learning processes in adolescence and tests whether two single session interventions (SSI) delivered in VR improve interoceptive functioning. METHODS: Ninety adolescents (60 with psychiatric disorders associated with interoceptive impairments and 30 unaffected healthy controls) between 12 and 17 years of age will complete a structured diagnostic clinical interview and an assessment battery of questionnaires to characterize the presence of psychiatric disorders, severity of psychiatric symptoms, interoceptive awareness, and related constructs (e.g., sleep, distress tolerance, mindfulness, self-efficacy). Youth will complete validated tasks to assess interoceptive functioning (e.g., cardiac interoceptive accuracy, interoceptive awareness of heart rate) and two associative learning mechanisms (e.g., aversive conditioning and reward learning). While cardiac interoception will serve as the primary outcome measure of interoceptive functioning, secondary outcomes of other systems will be explored (e.g., temporal coupling between gastric rhythms and neural activity). Finally, participants will complete two SSIs in VR (i.e., mindfulness, relaxation training) to examine effects on interoceptive accuracy and awareness. RESULTS: Participant enrollment began in December 2024. Currently, 45 participants have enrolled in study protocol. Participants are 15.3 ± 1.7 years of age on average with a nearly equal distribution of boys and girls. At this time, there are no differences in demographic characteristics between adolescents with and without psychiatric conditions. CONCLUSIONS: Findings will provide novel insights about interoception in adolescence and clarify its role in the development and maintenance of psychiatric disorders. It will provide preliminary evidence on the feasibility and effectiveness of brief VR-based mindfulness and relaxation interventions targeting interoception, helping to inform future early intervention strategies for at-risk youth. papers.title: Cognitive impairment in glaucoma.
papers.abstract: Glaucoma, while regarded as an isolated ocular disorder, is now increasingly recognized as a component of a wider neurological spectrum. An accumulating body of neuroimaging-based studies have revealed structural and functional changes in the brain that are analogous to those observed in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease. These changes are further associated with systemic disturbances, including autonomic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and elevated cortisol levels. This mounting evidence may elucidate the increased susceptibility of cognitive impairment and dementia observed in individuals with glaucoma. This article presents a narrative review of the existing literature. A thorough search was conducted across various databases, including PubMed, Scopus, and the Embase Library, without restriction on year of publication. This review consolidates various lines of evidence that underscore the common characteristic between glaucomatous optic neuropathy and neurodegenerative disorders. A range of pharmacological (anti-dementia medication, nootropic agent, cerebral metabolizers, and neutraceuticals) and nonpharmacological strategies (regular physical activity, meditation, sleep optimization, and dietary modification) and emerging modalities-including noninvasive brain stimulation, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems, and artificial intelligence-guided therapeutic models-are broadening the scope of management beyond traditional approaches that not only target intraocular pressure reduction but also may support overall neuro-cognitive wellbeing. The establishment of a multidisciplinary framework is also vital, wherein an ophthalmologist works in collaboration with neurologists, psychologists, and rehabilitation specialists to facilitate thorough cognitive evaluation and timely treatment. This review underscores the need of safeguarding both visual and cognitive functions by recognizing glaucoma as an ocular disorder and neurodegenerative condition, aiming to improve long-term outcomes and quality of life.
